react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by a coordinated eicosanoid-shock signal spanning three paradigm calls. Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) is the top RaMP hit (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, fold enrichment 1 430×, 5 of 8 inputs present: arachidonate C00219, leukotriene A4 C00909, 5-HETE C04805, 15-HETE C04742, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 C14717). The same module maps to Mummichog's Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM, p = 9.24 × 10⁻⁴, overlap = 11/11 matched to a 11-compound pathway), and MetaboAnalystR's Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (p = 0.036). Arachidonic acid itself (KEGG:C00219) sits at the apex of all three: it is the substrate entry point for 5-lipoxygenase (producing LTA4 and the LTB4/LTC4 cascade), for COX-1/2 (producing PGD2 → 15d-PGJ2), and for CYP450 / 12/15-lipoxygenase (producing 5- and 15-HETE). The Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6 inputs including L-cysteine C00097 and L-cystathionine C02291) captures the secondary sulfur-amino cluster; MetaboAnalystR independently confirms this via KEGG:hsa00670 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism, p = 0.0051) and hsa00270 (p = 0.0082). L-cysteine is the canonical co-substrate for GSH synthesis and for the 5-lipoxygenase activating protein (FLAP), linking the two major pathway clusters. Mercaptopurine (KEGG:C02380) was not captured by any pathway-enrichment tool — it is a purine antimetabolite whose differential abundance likely reflects a pharmacologic intervention rather than endogenous eicosanoid or sulfur metabolism. The three-way paradigm consensus (ORA + m/z-direct + PSEA) on eicosanoid synthesis is robust: five driver lipids share arachidonic acid as the biochemical origin, and their coordinated dysregulation is biologically coherent with oxidative/inflammatory challenge or COX/LOX inhibition.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools — run_ramp_enrichment (RaMP multi-DB ORA), run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG PSEA), and run_mummichog (mass-network paradigm) — all converge on Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top hit across paradigms. run_mummichog reports MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism at p=0.0017 with all 11 matched metabolites from the input set (overlap 11/11). run_ramp_enrichment reports WP:WP167 "Eicosanoid synthesis" at FDR 6.18×10⁻¹⁴ (fold enrichment 1430×) with five lipid input metabolites: arachidonic acid (C00219, CHEBI:15843), leukotriene A4 (C00909, CHEBI:15651), 5(S)-HETE (C04805, CHEBI:28209), 15(S)-HETE (C04742, CHEBI:15558), and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²·¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 (C14717, CHEBI:34159). KEGG hsa00590 via run_metaboanalystr_psea independently hits the same four canonical eicosanoid metabolites (arachidonic acid, LTA4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). Secondary convergence on cysteine and methionine metabolism is supported by cystathionine (C02291, CHEBI:17482) and L-cysteine (C00097, CHEBI:17561) across mummichog (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism, p=0.054, overlap 2/2) and KEGG hsa00670 (p=0.0051), with the latter also connecting to the Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR 6.18×10⁻¹⁴, 6 input metabolites). 15-deoxy-Δ¹²·¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 hits only the RaMP/WikiPathways eicosanoid result (not KEGG or mummichog networks), reflecting its status as a cyclopentenone downstream of non-COXP450 branches. Mercaptopurine (C02380) is not assigned to any enriched pathway in any tool, suggesting primary metabolic context in purine pathways outside the observed lipid and sulfur amino acid signal. The three-tool consensus on arachidonic acid metabolism is robust across ORA and network paradigms, establishing a biological signal consistent with inflammatory eicosanoid biosynthesis and associated transsulfuration flux.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by a coordinated eicosanoid-shock signal spanning three paradigm calls. Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) is the top RaMP hit (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, fold enrichment 1 430×, 5 of 8 inputs present: arachidonate C00219, leukotriene A4 C00909, 5-HETE C04805, 15-HETE C04742, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 C14717). The same module maps to Mummichog's Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM, p = 9.24 × 10⁻⁴, overlap = 11/11 matched to a 11-compound pathway), and MetaboAnalystR's Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (p = 0.036). Arachidonic acid itself (KEGG:C00219) sits at the apex of all three: it is the substrate entry point for 5-lipoxygenase (producing LTA4 and the LTB4/LTC4 cascade), for COX-1/2 (producing PGD2 → 15d-PGJ2), and for CYP450 / 12/15-lipoxygenase (producing 5- and 15-HETE). The Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6 inputs including L-cysteine C00097 and L-cystathionine C02291) captures the secondary sulfur-amino cluster; MetaboAnalystR independently confirms this via KEGG:hsa00670 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism, p = 0.0051) and hsa00270 (p = 0.0082). L-cysteine is the canonical co-substrate for GSH synthesis and for the 5-lipoxygenase activating protein (FLAP), linking the two major pathway clusters. Mercaptopurine (KEGG:C02380) was not captured by any pathway-enrichment tool — it is a purine antimetabolite whose differential abundance likely reflects a pharmacologic intervention rather than endogenous eicosanoid or sulfur metabolism. The three-way paradigm consensus (ORA + m/z-direct + PSEA) on eicosanoid synthesis is robust: five driver lipids share arachidonic acid as the biochemical origin, and their coordinated dysregulation is biologically coherent with oxidative/inflammatory challenge or COX/LOX inhibition.
